title: HarvestLink · From harvest to a human-approved deal
text: Fresh harvests need buyers. Restaurant kitchens need reliable supplies. HarvestLink connects those needs through farmer-led trading, inventory foresight, and bounded agent negotiation.

title: 01 / FARMER · A private workspace
text: The farmer signs in to a separate account and completes a simple profile. Ananya Farms keeps its own harvest listings and private selling rules. Each restaurant has an independent buying workspace.

title: Actual Excel workbook → preview → every validated harvest row
text: Here is the actual farmer harvest Excel workbook. The upload reads the first worksheet and previews its rows before import. Crop, variety, grade, quantity, price and availability stay visible. After validation, all workbook rows become harvest listings. No manual database editing is needed.

title: Separate mandi report · Source, date and units stay visible
text: Mandi prices have their own report. Here, twenty-four cached government records carry their source and nineteenth October reporting date. The farmer can inspect market, commodity and units. Reported prices are benchmarks, not guaranteed selling rates.

title: The farmer sets the boundaries
text: The grower sets a private minimum price, minimum order quantity and nearby service radius. Those rules constrain negotiation. They do not authorize a sale: the farmer always makes the final buyer selection.

title: Kannada workspace · Madhu with actual Sarvam speech
text: Madhu answers in Kannada. Hear the app’s actual Sarvam voice response.

title: Next-crop planning · Explainable scenarios
text: Next-crop planning combines the planting date, water availability, rotation context and restaurant usage. The farmer can inspect candidate crops and change the water assumption. These are transparent planning scenarios, not guaranteed demand or locally validated growing advice.

title: 02 / RESTAURANT · Forecast consumption, account for expiry
text: The Green Table opens its own inventory view. Amazon Chronos Two forecasts consumption from synthetic usage history. Separate inventory logic accounts for usable batches and incoming orders, then recommends replenishment. The evaluation shows both model and baseline errors honestly; the model is not assumed to win.

title: Buyer limits → an approved purchase requirement
text: The restaurant sets its maximum price and total budget, reviews the suggested quantity, and approves a purchase requirement. The marketplace connects that requirement to farmer listings. Forecasting supports a decision; it never silently spends money.

title: Actual AI offers · Replay, price chart and farmer choice
text: Three restaurant agents submit proposals within their own limits. The replay presents the actual recorded negotiation steps, while the price chart makes changes easy to compare. These are model-assisted offers, checked by server rules. The farmer reviews quantity, price and collection terms, then explicitly chooses The Green Table. The system does not pick a winner on the farmer's behalf.

title: Mutual agreement → stock reservation → simulated escrow
text: The selected restaurant reviews the same agreement and confirms it. Stock is reserved only after confirmation. Funding moves the order into a clearly labelled simulated escrow state. The agreement animation and funded amount show this change visually. No real money moves, and funding is separate from the farmer's selection.

title: Leaflet delivery simulation · Receipt and settlement
text: The farmer records collection and plays the delivery simulation on the Leaflet map. The moving vehicle follows an illustrative route, not live GPS. The restaurant confirms receipt, adding the delivered produce to inventory. Finally, the farmer releases simulated funds, completing the visible agreement-to-delivery journey.

title: HarvestLink · Better-informed trade. Human decisions.
text: Farmer choice. Kitchen foresight. Clear agreements. One connected HarvestLink workflow.
